Make Nostr easy to spot

Two design directions for MyEditor, shown on every Nostr surface in the app. Both follow one rule: whatever belongs to your Nostr account carries violet, and everything that stays on your Mac keeps the look it has today.

Direction
Appearance

Your editor on the left, the Imports window on the right. The editor stays the editor; its Nostr tab, the Drafts panel and the account capsule carry violet. The Imports window is Nostr through and through.

What the research says

Other apps had the same problem: one window, two worlds. Here is what worked, what failed, and what it means for MyEditor.

Safari Private Browsing

Private mode is set per window. Its constant cue is a dark Smart Search field; older versions also printed a line of text at the top of the window.

A mode needs both color and words. One small dark field is easy to miss when several windows are open.Apple Safari guide, Intego

Firefox Containers

Container tabs began with a colored line. Firefox 89 shrank the color down to the icon, and people could no longer tell work tabs from personal ones. Firefox 155 now colors the whole tab.

Hairlines and tinted icons fail. Color needs area.Mozilla blog, bug 1714903, bug 2058198

Arc and browser profiles

Arc lets every profile theme the browser frame in its own colors and shows the profile's icon. Users call the result very discernible, and Firefox answers requests for colored windows with per-profile themes.

Tint the frame, and show who is signed in.Orion feedback thread, Mozilla Connect

AppKit on macOS 26

Apple's new design tints prominent toolbar items with the accent color, or any color through backgroundTintColor, to show state. Glass is kept for controls; titles and status indicators stay flat.

Violet belongs on controls and on calm, flat surfaces, not on decorative glass.WWDC25, Build an AppKit app with the new design

Nostr clients

For many people purple already means Nostr. Amethyst, one of the large clients, moved from a warm purple to a purple-to-blue gradient.

Use a violet that leans slightly blue, so it reads as Nostr and never as the magenta of the macOS Purple accent.Amethyst logo proposal

Shared by both directions

Violet means it belongs to your Nostr account: it gets signed, synced or published. Everything that stays on your Mac keeps the normal look.

The relay mark. A point that sends: notes carried by relays. It sits next to every Nostr title, tab and status, so color is never the only cue. This is a proposal; the final mark is yours to choose.

Nostr Violet leans slightly blue, away from the macOS Purple accent (#953D96). White labels on 500 and 600 reach about 6:1.

Color says where you are. Words say what happens.

Every Nostr surface names the account and the result, in the app's own voice: Auf 3 Relays gesichert, Wird mit deinem Schlüssel signiert, Personen auf Nostr. The account capsule shows who is signed in on every Nostr surface, the way browsers show the active profile.

Night Violet

Nostr is a place. Open a Nostr window and its whole frame turns night violet, the way Safari Private turns dark. Only the content in the middle stays plain.

Imports. Title bar, toolbar, sources and the post list share one violet material, with a soft light in the top corner. The article preview keeps the neutral background, because it is content.

The editor. Your page and your folders look exactly as today. The Drafts panel becomes a small violet room beside the page, the Nostr tab is tinted from edge to edge, and the status bar names where the draft lives.

Tab and account. The whole tab is tinted, as Firefox learned the hard way.

Save. Only the Nostr card is violet; the button follows your choice. Click a card.

Mentions. The picker floats in the night material over your neutral page.

How it works

  • The frame is the material. Title bar, toolbar, sidebars and lists share one violet-tinted surface, so a Nostr window reads as one object.
  • Tinted grays. Text and hairlines carry a trace of violet too, which keeps the material calm instead of painted on.
  • Light from one corner. A single soft glow sits in the top corner; nothing else is a gradient except the default button.
  • Content stays paper. Article previews and your writing keep the neutral background.

Trade-offs

The strongest signal at a glance and the closest to your users' own idea. Inside the editor the violet panel weighs more than the page next to it, and in Light mode the material turns lavender, softer and less striking than in Dark.

Building it in Qt

Flat colors, plus qlineargradient and qradialgradient in the style sheets. No blur, no custom painting.

Horizon

Nostr is a light source. Every Nostr surface carries a violet horizon along its top edge that fades into the normal app. The same signature on a window, a panel, a tab or a popover.

Imports. Violet light rises from the top of the window, sealed by a thin bright edge, and fades out across sources and posts. Below it the window keeps the system grays.

The editor. The Drafts panel, the Nostr tab and the mention picker each start with the same horizon. Your page stays white or dark gray from edge to edge.

Tab and account. The tab fills with the horizon and gets its bright top edge.

Save. The Nostr card glows from its top; the button follows your choice. Click a card.

Mentions. Even a small popover carries the signature in its header.

How it works

  • One signature at every size. Windows, side panels, tabs and popovers all begin with the same glow, so the eye learns one shape.
  • The top edge, where the eye lands first. Below it, every surface returns to the system grays.
  • Solid violet controls. Selections and default buttons are flat violet, like the tinted prominent buttons of macOS 26.
  • A sealed edge. A one-pixel bright line on top makes the glow read as light, not as a stain.

Trade-offs

Feels native and keeps the editor clean for people who never use Nostr. On very short surfaces, such as a single row, the horizon has no room to show; there the relay mark carries the signal alone.

Building it in Qt

One qlineargradient per Nostr surface plus a one-pixel top border. Nothing else changes in the existing style sheets.

Every Nostr surface

MyEditor has more than sixty places where Nostr shows up. Here are the ones the first sheet left out, from Blossom media to the EINUNDZWANZIG membership, drawn in either direction. The complete list closes the section.

Direction

Blossom media

Your Mediathek lives on Blossom servers, so the whole library is Nostr. In the document, a badge tells whether a picture is still only on this computer or already on your media servers; that is the rule at its most useful, because it answers the question "who can see this?".

Mediathek. The selected file, the upload ring and the account capsule carry violet. Pictures stay exactly as they are; private files keep their lock, failed uploads stay red with „Wiederholen“.

Medienserver. A sheet on the Mediathek. The main server is the selected row; the membership server is named as such.

Media in your text. „Auf diesem Computer“ keeps the dark capsule, because the file is local. Uploading and uploaded turn violet; failed stays red. Audio and video cards show their upload as a violet line.

Profile and account

Your profile and your keys belong to your Nostr account. The profile card shows you as others see you, so it stays neutral like any content. Connecting a signer, creating, backing up, restoring and moving a key share one step window: step badges turn violet as they complete, and the waiting line names what MyEditor waits for. Codes stay dark on white, so every wallet and signer can read them.

Profil bearbeiten. Material or horizon around a neutral profile card; the focused field gets the violet ring.

Signer-App verbinden. The same step layout carries „Konto erstellen“, „Konto sichern“, „Konto wiederherstellen“ and „Schlüssel in Signer-App verschieben“.

EINUNDZWANZIG: violet meets orange

The membership is both: it belongs to your Nostr account, and it is EINUNDZWANZIG and Bitcoin. So its windows speak both colors, each with a clear job, and they meet in one dusk gradient.

Nostr VioletYour account: the frame, selections, the default button.
DuskWhere they meet: the membership card, the service tiles, the glow or horizon of the window.
Bitcoin orangeEINUNDZWANZIG and money: the brand, Lightning payments, amounts.

Mitgliederseite. The card turns from violet into orange, every service tile follows it, and the window adds an orange glow (Night Violet) or a horizon that turns from violet to orange (Horizon). „Fertig“ stays violet: it is an account action.

Bezahlen. Money is orange: the amount, the frame around the Lightning code, the checking line and „Ich habe bezahlt“. The code itself stays dark on white so every wallet reads it. The same orange tag marks the membership server in „Medienserver“.

Publishing

The publish sheets are where content leaves your Mac, so they say it twice: with violet, and with words naming the account and the signer.

Als Artikel veröffentlichen. The preview card on the left is content and stays neutral. Hashtags, people and „Veröffentlichen als“ carry violet; the status line names the signer while it waits. „Als Notiz veröffentlichen“ and „Als Nostr-Entwurf speichern“ follow the same layout.

Writing an article

The article header sits inside your document, so it only gains a small line with the relay mark. Article Details is a side panel and gets the full treatment, like Drafts. A newer version from another device appears as a violet banner on top of the page.

Article header, Artikeldetails and the conflict banner. The inspector toggle in the toolbar is tinted while the panel is open, so you see where it came from.

Notiz oder Artikel einfügen. A popover at the caret, like the mention picker.

Importfortschritt. The job card from the Imports toolbar, with a violet bar.

Status bar. Nostr results carry the relay mark and violet ink; everything else stays gray.

Alerts, mixed and system surfaces

Some places are not Nostr's alone. Settings shows two Nostr rows only while an account is in use; they get the relay mark and nothing more. Menus and the Dock number are drawn by macOS and stay untouched; the menu title already says Nostr.

Einstellungen. The relay mark tells which two rows belong to Nostr.

Alerts. The app icon carries the relay mark and the default action is violet. Destructive buttons such as „Löschen“ stay red.

Nostr menu. System-drawn, so no tint, in either direction.

One rule per kind of surface

Every Nostr surface falls into one of ten kinds. Each kind gets one treatment, so the code needs ten rules, not sixty designs.

In both: a dusk card and dusk service tiles, Bitcoin orange for the brand, Lightning payments and amounts, violet for account actions.

Choosing

My recommendation: Horizon as the system

One signature covers all three places Nostr appears: its own windows, its pieces inside the editor, and mixed dialogs. It keeps the editor clean for people who never touch Nostr, and it stays readable in Light and Dark alike.

If the Imports and Profile windows should feel like a separate place, Night Violet's material can be used for those full windows only, with Horizon everywhere else. The two share every color, so they combine without friction.

Still open

  1. The direction: Night Violet, Horizon, or Horizon with Night Violet for full Nostr windows. Section “Every Nostr surface” shows both on all of them.
  2. The mark: the relay mark here is a proposal.
  3. Light mode strength: both directions are tuned softer in Light; check them on your own screen.
  4. EINUNDZWANZIG: violet for the account, orange for the brand and payments, dusk where they meet (as shown).
  5. Media badges: violet for files on your media servers, the dark capsule for files only on this computer (as shown).
